title: Article II, section 2, clause 2: appointments
summary: Article II provides the default appointment process and the permitted alternatives for inferior officers.
notes:
The President nominates and, with Senate advice and consent, appoints ambassadors, other public ministers and consuls, Supreme Court judges, and other officers whose appointments are not otherwise provided for and whose offices are established by law. Congress may by law vest appointment of inferior officers in the President alone, courts of law, or department heads.

First determine whether the position is an office, then whether it is principal or inferior, then whether the chosen appointing actor is constitutionally permitted and statutorily authorized. The clause does not require Senate approval for every employee and does not itself let Congress appoint officers.
